subject: The Go To Position dialog's window title on a de-DE Logic
question: What is the Go To Position dialog called in German, and why did the census not have it?

reverify.expected: `Zu Position|AXFloatingWindow;` on a German Logic; the menu path is tried in every measured spelling, so the same script answers on en-US, ko-KR and ja-JP with their own titles
reverify.cost: needs Logic open on any project; ~10 s, opens the dialog and closes it with Escape

method: Navigate ▸ Go To ▸ Position… was opened through the menu, each segment matched against the spellings the policy declares rather than a translated one, and every non-standard window was listed with its subrole. Escape closed the dialog; nothing was submitted, so the playhead did not move. Run twice to distinguish a title from a one-off.

observations.what: first open: the only non-standard window and its subrole
observations.title: Zu Position

observations.what: what the product reported before the variant existed
the navigation-free census of the same day, searched for this string

conclusion: On this host in German the dialog is titled `Zu Position`, the same string on both opens, on an AXFloatingWindow. It occurs 0 times in the 2026-09-12 de-DE navigation-free census, because that census opens nothing — which is why the label was missing and why the product answered `dialog_unidentified_new_window` rather than naming the window it had just caused to appear.
limits: One dialog. Every other German dialog title is still unmeasured, and they are unmeasurable the same way — a navigation-free census cannot reach any of them.
One host and one build. A Logic update can rename a dialog without renaming the menu item that opens it.
It says what the window is CALLED, not that dismissing it by that name works — the product's use of this label is to recognise a stale dialog, and this record does not exercise that path.
